notice: Corrections to claims made in receipts/W09/W09-01/receipt.json. That file is byte-frozen: the reviewer read and hashed it, so nothing in it is edited. What the receipt said at the moment it was written is left standing here as the record of when each inaccuracy existed.
trigger: independent_review.json verdict ACCEPT_WITH_LIMITATIONS, problems P1-P4, limitations L1-L14

corrections.what_the_receipt_said: 'one mutant per leg of a compound guard, learned from W08-01's round-1 review; whole-condition flips were what let six legs pass unasserted there.' with mutation_matrix {caught: 8} and survivors_and_uncatched []
corrections.what_is_true: Five of the eight rows (N01, N02, N03, N03b, N05) are genuine single legs. Three are not: N04 and N06 rewrite `A != X || B != Y` as `if B != Y && false {`, and N07 rewrites `data == nil || Digest(data) != hash` as `if data == nil && false {`. Each `&& false` disables BOTH operands of a disjunction at once, which is precisely the shape the same sentence names as the W08-01 defect. So {caught: 8} is accurate about the eight rows I ran and `survivors_and_uncatched: []` is accurate about those rows, and neither is a statement about the legs of the guards. Coverage of legs must be read from the reviewer's independent battery, not from this field.
corrections.verification: Read directly from the card's frozen mutation driver at receipts/W09/W09-01/mut_w0901_round1.py (sha256 c0362484f11f4bbc..., byte-identical to the .local working copy); the replacement strings are lines 50, 58 and 62 and are quoted above. Independently reproduced by the reviewer: single-leg mutants R03 and R06 (N07's two operands), O02 and O04 (N04/N06's operands) each left all 41 assertions green, and only the paired mutant P01, removing both N07 operands, went red on W0901-SEARCH-REVALIDATES-CURRENT-SOURCE-HASH-BEFORE-HIT.
corrections.aggravating_fact: The per-leg rule was on the page when I broke it. The comment I wrote on the immediately preceding row N03b reads: 'The hash half of the same compound is a different decision and needs its own mutant and its own input.' The failure was not ignorance of the rule but stopping at the row that compiled.

corrections.what_the_receipt_said: That id appears as the evidence line for the three named counterexamples (SIMULATED presented as OBSERVED, cross-project same-name capture, cache hit after revocation).
corrections.what_is_true: The row compares the expected counterexample rows against the emitted set, so whenever the roster guard already fired it can only be red as a consequence of the same fact. Removing the group's positive control W0901-SEALED-BODY-SERVED-BEFORE-REVOCATION entirely (reviewer mutant H13) left it GREEN. It therefore has no independent discriminating power. The real witnesses are the 17 individual product-path rows, which the reviewer verified refusing at the product path with asserted status, code and message, and with every secret marker appearing zero times.
corrections.consequence: A future reader must not treat this id as proof that the counterexamples are guarded. It is proof that a set of ids was emitted.

corrections.what_the_receipt_said: That the handler resolves go only from the locked table and refuses a PATH fallback.
corrections.what_is_true: The assertion feeds resolve_go a nonexistent absolute path and the bare string 'go'. Both fail before the locked sha256 comparison, the version_output comparison and the isabs requirement are reached, so blinding each of those three legs (reviewer mutants H09, H10, H11) left all 41 ids green. The digest leg is the only guard against a RESEARCHOS_GO that points at a real but wrong binary, and this roster does not assert it.
corrections.what_remains_proved: The behaviour itself is correct and was re-established independently by the reviewer with decoy probes: RESEARCHOS_GO aimed at python.exe and at git.exe returned None and named the digest mismatch; a bare 'go', a relative path and an unset variable each resolved to the pinned go1.27.1 by hash and version and never to PATH; no PATH entry on this host contains a go.exe. This correction is about test pinning, not about a wrong runtime outcome.

corrections.what_the_review_measured: 796 directories under execution/v2.4/receipts/W09/W09-01/dispatched/, described as '752 of them untracked; only 44 are committed'.
corrections.what_I_re_measured: 796 first-level directories: 694 are EMPTY and 102 are non-empty. Across them, 173 files are tracked and 232 are untracked. The reviewer's 752 is git's collapsed count from `git ls-files --others --directory`, which lists an empty directory as one untracked entry, so it is a true count of entries and an overstatement of untracked content by roughly 3.2x on files and 5.3x on bytes.
corrections.root_cause: serve() creates the uuid4 directory before it knows whether the run will produce anything, so every refused-binding dispatch and every mutant that aborts before the first write leaves an empty directory behind. The accumulation is mine and it is a defect of this card's handler, not of the dispatcher.
corrections.disposition: Left in place, not deleted: some of these directories are evidence the product itself wrote under the reviewer's runs, and mass-deleting another identity's outputs is not mine to do. Registered as an obligation for the card that owns the handler to create the directory lazily, immediately before its first write.

claims_i_withdrew_without_being_asked: Nothing in this file disputes the reviewer's positive findings. Where its numbers are corrected (C-4) the correction reduces the severity of a finding against my own card, so it is stated with the measuring command in the same sentence.
what_this_card_still_proves: The 31 W0901-* product assertions and the routing refusals were reproduced by an independent identity: three bound dispatches agreed on 41 unique ids, the two routing refusals exit 3 with zero assertions, and 18 of the reviewer's own single-leg mutants killed on exactly the id that names them. The implementation is not in question; three sentences in my receipt over-described it.
